hero.headline: Flesh-eating cattle parasite spreads beyond Texas as screwworm cases rise
hero.body:
A parasitic fly that feeds on living flesh has been detected in cattle in Texas, marking the first cases in the United States since the 1960s. The New World screwworm, eradicated from the country decades ago, has triggered an aggressive federal and state response aimed at preventing further spread.

The first case was confirmed in a three-week-old calf with an umbilical lesion in Zavala County, southwest of San Antonio. A second infection was discovered days later in a one-year-old calf approximately five miles away. The Texas Animal Health Commission established an infested zone in the area and implemented animal movement restrictions to contain the parasite.

The New World screwworm is a parasitic larva that burrows through the living flesh of warm-blooded animals and humans, causing a painful condition called myiasis. If left untreated, the infection can be fatal to infected animals.

Texas Governor Greg Abbott issued a statewide disaster declaration in response to the outbreak. "We're in the season for spread," Abbott warned, predicting an "extraordinarily challenging summer" for affected areas. State officials are coordinating with the federal government to slow the parasite's expansion.

The response includes releasing millions of sterile screwworm flies near the infection sites. These sterile male flies cannot reproduce with wild females, which prevents the population from expanding. The U.S. Department of Agriculture has deployed teams and is testing suspect cases to identify additional infections. Officials emphasized that this combination of sterile fly release, enhanced surveillance, movement restrictions, prompt wound treatment, and public education represents a proven and effective control strategy.

The Texas Animal Health Commission had spent more than two years preparing for a potential resurgence of the parasite. "We are putting these preparations into action, and we encourage all animal owners and caretakers to continue to remain vigilant for the presence of larvae in animal wounds and immediately report any suspicions," said commission director Dr Bud Dinges.

A widespread outbreak could significantly impact the U.S. cattle industry. The country has faced economic pressures since the disease appeared in Central America more than a year ago. The U.S.-Mexico border has been closed to live cattle imports during this period, shrinking the roughly 100 billion dollar beef industry to a 75-year low. The United States formerly imported more than one million cattle annually from Mexico, representing approximately 4 to 5 percent of all cattle sold for beef production.

Canada's food inspection agency announced a temporary ban on livestock from Texas, prohibiting cattle and horses that were in the state within 21 days before crossing the border. Though officials noted the parasite is unlikely to establish itself in Canada's colder climate, they warned farmers to monitor livestock for wounds accompanied by discharge or foul odor.

The USDA confirmed that the U.S. food supply remains safe, as the screwworm does not infest meat, fruits, vegetables, or other food sources.

cards.headline: Israel and Iran Pause Strikes After Trump Claims Progress on Nuclear Talks
cards.body:
Israel and Iran have halted military operations following an exchange of strikes, with President Trump claiming progress toward nuclear negotiations has influenced the decision to stand down.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that Israel's military actions are temporarily suspended after speaking with Trump. Iran's armed forces also confirmed they have stopped their attacks. Both nations, however, signaled they remain prepared to resume hostilities if the ceasefire is violated.

The pause follows what sources described as a significant 15-hour exchange of strikes between the two countries. Trump had urged Netanyahu not to respond to Iran's attacks, telling reporters that he did not want escalation to derail ongoing negotiations. "I'm about to call Bibi right now and tell him not to respond. Both of them have already done their part. Israel had its strike and Iran had its strike. We don't need another one," Trump said.

Initially, Netanyahu continued military action despite Trump's calls for restraint. The Israeli military confirmed it struck military targets in western and central Iran, though it provided no further details. Trump subsequently warned Netanyahu that Israel would be "on your own" if attacks on Iran continued. The White House did not immediately confirm whether the Israeli strikes were coordinated with the United States.

Trump has repeatedly claimed progress toward a deal with Iran, telling Axios that he is concerned escalation could jeopardize negotiations. "I don't want it to blow up because of what's happening now," Trump said.

The escalating strikes had raised concerns about a wider regional conflict engulfing the Middle East. The temporary pause creates space for potential diplomatic progress on nuclear talks, though the fragility of the ceasefire remains evident.

Iran appears emboldened by the outcome of the exchange. According to BBC analysis, Iran's decision to proceed with strikes despite potential damage to peace talks may reflect how its leaders view their current position. The missile exchange demonstrated the constraints facing both sides and exposed the challenges Trump faces in managing his relationship with Netanyahu while pursuing negotiations with Tehran.

Iran's parliament speaker and top negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, stated that US bases and assets in the region had become "legitimate targets" following the Israeli strike on southern Beirut in Lebanon.

Both countries have maintained their military capability and expressed willingness to resume operations if they determine violations have occurred. Netanyahu specifically said strikes were on hold "at the moment," emphasizing the conditional nature of the ceasefire.

The situation continues to evolve as Trump pursues negotiations with Iran while attempting to prevent further escalation in the region.

cards.headline: NATO Shoots Down Drone Over Latvia as Ukraine War Spillover Concerns Grow
cards.teaser: A French fighter jet operating under NATO command shot down a drone in Latvian airspace, extending fears about the Ukraine war spreading beyond its borders.
cards.body:
NATO jets shot down a drone over Latvian airspace in an incident that underscores growing concerns about the Ukraine conflict spreading beyond its borders. A French aircraft on NATO patrol intercepted and destroyed the unmanned aircraft. Latvia attributed the incident to Russian electronic warfare.

The shootdown represents another instance of the war's effects reaching NATO territory. The incident has prompted heightened security measures and intensified NATO's vigilance along its eastern flank as the conflict continues.

cards.headline: Republican senators warn surveillance law may lapse over Trump intelligence nominee
cards.teaser: Republican lawmakers hope Trump will withdraw his intelligence director nominee to preserve a key surveillance program facing expiration.
cards.body:
Republican senators warned that a major surveillance program may lapse after backlash over President Trump's nominee for Director of National Intelligence, Andrew Pulte. Senate Majority Leader John Thune urged passage of a FISA extension before the deadline amid the controversy surrounding the nomination.

Democratic opposition to Pulte has put reauthorization of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act in jeopardy, creating a bipartisan obstacle to renewing the spy program. Republicans are hoping Trump will reconsider the nomination to salvage the intelligence law before it expires.

cards.headline: Federal judge strikes down Trump administration's $100,000 H-1B visa fee
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled the administration's requirement for employers to pay a $100,000 fee for H-1B highly skilled worker visas unlawful.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Boston has invalidated Donald Trump's $100,000 annual fee on H-1B visa applications, ruling it an unlawful tax that violated federal administrative law and the constitution. The decision came in a lawsuit filed by 20 Democratic state attorneys general challenging the fee Trump announced in September.

The fee represented a dramatic increase—20 to 50 times higher than existing rates—for employers seeking to hire foreign workers in specialty occupations. The Trump administration is expected to appeal the ruling.

cards.headline: Pentagon adds Alibaba, BYD and Baidu to Chinese military company list
cards.body:
The Pentagon has designated Chinese tech giant Alibaba, electric vehicle manufacturer BYD, and search engine Baidu as companies with alleged ties to China's military, according to the Trump administration's updated list released four months ago. The designation serves as a warning to American businesses about potential risks associated with working with these flagged companies.

The list identifies Chinese entities believed to support the People's Liberation Army or China's defense industrial base. Pharmaceutical company WuXi AppTec also appears on the expanded catalog. The Pentagon uses this list as an advisory tool to highlight companies that US officials believe operate in support of Chinese military modernization efforts.

While the designation does not directly impose sanctions or prohibit transactions, it signals regulatory risks and increased scrutiny for American firms maintaining commercial relationships with listed companies. The list guides US businesses and investors in their decision-making regarding potential partnerships or investments involving these Chinese corporations.

Some companies have appeared and disappeared from the Pentagon's catalog in previous versions. The restoration of major names like Alibaba and Baidu to the current list reflects shifting dynamics in US-China economic relations, potentially affecting recent diplomatic efforts between Washington and Beijing.

The timing adds pressure to Chinese companies already navigating complex international trade restrictions. BYD, one of the world's largest electric vehicle makers, has been expanding its global sales outside the United States. Meanwhile, Alibaba and Baidu remain dominant forces in Chinese technology and cloud computing sectors.

Notably, the Trump administration released the updated list four months ago but then quickly removed it without providing an explanation for the decision. The subsequent restoration of these companies to the list marks a significant shift in policy direction.

The Pentagon designation could influence how these companies approach investment decisions and partnerships as they operate within an increasingly fragmented global technology landscape. For BYD specifically, the listing may complicate its efforts to expand electric vehicle operations internationally, despite the company's position as a global leader in EV manufacturing.

The inclusion of these major technology and manufacturing firms on the military-linked companies list underscores ongoing tensions in the US-China technology competition. As American officials continue evaluating which Chinese companies pose risks to US national security interests, businesses on both sides of the Pacific face uncertainty regarding future commercial relationships and regulatory requirements.

The Pentagon has not provided detailed explanations regarding the specific military connections attributed to each company on the list. The companies themselves have not publicly responded to their designations.

cards.headline: Russian satellites can jam GPS across continental distances, tests indicate
cards.teaser: Testing suggests Russian satellites possess the ability to interfere with GPS signals on a continental scale.
cards.body:
Tests have shown that Russian satellites can jam GPS signals across continental distances, according to new findings. The discovery raises questions about Russian intentions and capabilities in space-based electronic warfare.

GPS interference has been detected across Europe in recent months, prompting investigations into the source and extent of the jamming. The tests suggest the interference originates from Russian satellite systems with the technical capability to disrupt navigation signals over vast geographic areas. The findings have implications for both civilian and military users of GPS technology.

cards.headline: Andy Burnham Runs for Parliament Seat in Campaign to Challenge Starmer
cards.teaser: The mayor of Greater Manchester is seeking a parliamentary seat in Makerfield in what analysts describe as a vital step toward ousting Prime Minister Keir Starmer.
cards.body:
Andy Burnham, the mayor of Greater Manchester, is running for a seat in Parliament in a by-election in Makerfield. The campaign represents a direct challenge to his Labour Party colleague Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Burnham's bid for the parliamentary seat is viewed as a necessary step in a broader effort to replace Starmer as party leader.

The by-election has drawn national attention because of its implications for Labour's internal politics. Burnham would need to win the seat and return to Parliament before he could mount a leadership challenge. The contest in Makerfield could determine whether Starmer faces a serious threat to his position as prime minister.

cards.headline: Peru Presidential Election Remains Close as Vote Counting Continues
cards.teaser: Right-wing candidate Keiko Fujimori and left-wing candidate Roberto Sánchez remain in a tight race as ballots are tallied in an election dominated by crime and instability concerns.
cards.body:
Peru's presidential election remains highly competitive as officials continue counting votes between right-wing candidate Keiko Fujimori and left-wing candidate Roberto Sánchez. The tight race reflects widespread voter concerns about crime and political instability affecting the nation.

The outcome will shape how Peru's next government addresses its most pressing challenges, particularly rising crime and the political turmoil that has destabilized the country in recent years.

cards.headline: International Criminal Court Chief Prosecutor Suspended Pending Sexual Misconduct Decision
cards.teaser: The ICC has suspended its chief prosecutor while an oversight body decides on sexual misconduct allegations against him.
cards.body:
The International Criminal Court has suspended chief prosecutor Karim Khan as disciplinary proceedings continue over sexual misconduct allegations. The ICC's Bureau announced the suspension following the investigation into the claims against Khan.

The ICC's oversight body will now determine the final outcome of the sexual misconduct case. Khan remains suspended from his role during this process.

cards.headline: Pope Warns of Global Spiritual and Cultural Crisis in Speech to Spanish Parliament
cards.teaser: Pope Leo delivered a historic address to Spain's parliament, warning of a profound global crisis and calling for respect for migrants.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV addressed Spain's parliament in Madrid, warning that the world faces a deep spiritual and cultural crisis. In his historic speech—the first papal address to the Spanish legislature—he urged the international community to address the causes and consequences of migration. The pontiff also discussed conflict, artificial intelligence, climate change, abortion, and euthanasia.

The pope called for moral renewal in legislatures and public life to ensure respect for the inherent dignity of all people. He emphasized that individuals must move beyond private faith and publicly witness to their beliefs through unity and diversity.

cards.headline: SpaceX Prepares for Stock Market Debut in Major Shift for Company
cards.teaser: SpaceX is preparing for a public offering that could transform the company, the broader market, and Elon Musk's personal fortune.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for a stock market debut that could transform the company, the wider market, and Elon Musk's fortune. The initial public offering would mark a significant departure from SpaceX's long-standing status as a privately held firm.

The move represents a major gamble for Musk, as going public would alter how the aerospace company operates and makes decisions about projects and investments. The listing could reshape SpaceX's financial structure and have broader implications across the market given the company's prominence in the aerospace sector.

cards.headline: Nithya Raman advances to runoff for Los Angeles mayor, defeating Spencer Pratt
cards.teaser: City council member Nithya Raman secured second place in the Los Angeles mayoral primary, ending reality television star Spencer Pratt's campaign.
cards.body:
Nithya Raman, a progressive Los Angeles city council member, has advanced to the November runoff for mayor after pulling ahead of Spencer Pratt during ballot counting. Raman will face incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in the general election.

Pratt, a former reality TV star from "The Hills," initially held a lead over Raman following last week's election. However, as the city continued processing ballots, Raman overtook him for the second spot. Pratt decided to run for mayor after his Pacific Palisades home was destroyed in the 2025 wildfires.

cards.headline: California gubernatorial race set between Becerra and Trump-backed candidate Hilton
cards.teaser: Updated vote counts show Attorney General Xavier Becerra will face Trump-endorsed candidate Hilton in the California governor's race.
cards.body:
California's gubernatorial primary results show Democrat Xavier Becerra securing the first spot in the general election, while Trump-backed Republican Steve Hilton was inching closer to the second runoff position. However, the race had yet to be officially called for Hilton, with more than 2.5 million ballots still left to be counted across the state.

As California continues its ballot counting process, Donald Trump and other Republicans have spread fraud claims about the election. These conspiracy theories have become common following California elections, though they lack evidence.

cards.teaser: Republican lawmakers hope Trump will withdraw his intelligence director nominee to preserve a key surveillance program facing expiration.

cards.headline: President Trump booed at NBA Finals appearance in New York
cards.teaser: Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to attend the NBA Finals, drawing catcalls from the Madison Square Garden crowd.
cards.body:
President Trump made history as the first sitting U.S. president to attend the NBA Finals, appearing at Game 3 between the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden. When he was shown on the jumbotron during the national anthem, sections of the crowd booed and jeered. Trump remained composed, maintaining a salute and smile during the roughly eight-second appearance.

The enhanced security measures at the arena reflected the presidential visit, with ticketholders required to pass through airport-style screening before entering Madison Square Garden.

cards.headline: SpaceX prepares stock market debut in potential transformation for Musk empire
cards.teaser: SpaceX is preparing to go public in a move that could reshape the company, the broader market, and Elon Musk's financial position.
cards.body:
SpaceX is moving toward a stock market debut that could reshape the company, Elon Musk's personal wealth and the broader markets. The space exploration company has remained private since its founding, with shares traded only among select investors.

A public offering would mark a significant shift in SpaceX's capital structure and represents one of Musk's most consequential financial decisions. Analysts view the potential debut as a major gamble that could fundamentally alter the landscape for both the company and the wider stock market.

cards.headline: OpenAI files for initial public offering
cards.teaser: The company behind ChatGPT submitted plans to go public one week after competitor Anthropic filed similar documents.
cards.body:
OpenAI has filed confidentially to go public on the US stock market, the company announced Monday. The ChatGPT maker is expected to become one of the most highly valued listings in market history, with a valuation exceeding $850 billion.

In its announcement, OpenAI noted that it has not yet decided on timing for the public debut. The company indicated it may remain private for a while longer, as certain objectives are easier to accomplish as a private company. OpenAI's IPO filing follows Anthropic's confidential submission the previous week, as major AI firms move toward public markets.

cards.headline: FCC waives Amazon satellite deployment deadline
cards.teaser: The commission lifted a looming deadline for Amazon's Leo broadband satellite constellation amid a shortage of available rockets.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission granted Amazon a waiver from its deadline to deploy satellites for its Leo broadband constellation, citing the public interest in developing a second major satellite internet network. The decision allows Amazon additional time to launch its planned satellites.

As a condition of the waiver, the FCC imposed a temporary spectrum penalty on the company. This approach lets Amazon proceed with its deployment schedule while maintaining its frequency licenses for the project.

cards.headline: SpaceX prepares for stock market debut
cards.teaser: The space company is moving toward an initial public offering that could significantly alter Elon Musk's wealth and the broader market.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for a stock market debut that could transform the company and significantly impact Elon Musk's personal wealth, given his major ownership stake in the privately held firm.

The public offering represents a major moment for both the aerospace and financial sectors, as SpaceX has established itself as a leader in commercial space operations with its dominant position in satellite launches and development of the Starship vehicle for future missions.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks over government stake in OpenAI
cards.teaser: The White House is discussing the possibility of the US government taking an ownership position in the artificial intelligence startup.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is negotiating with OpenAI about acquiring a government stake in the company, as part of efforts to gain a share of profits from the artificial intelligence sector.

Senator Bernie Sanders has proposed creating an AI sovereign wealth fund as an alternative method for public participation in AI industry gains.

cards.headline: Asian stock markets set for rebound on Iran developments and AI optimism
cards.teaser: Markets prepared to recover following positive developments in Iran negotiations and renewed confidence in artificial intelligence companies.
cards.body:
Asian stock markets positioned for gains following developments related to Iran and renewed optimism about AI sector companies. Chip-linked shares in the region showed signs of recovery after their US counterparts bounced back in trading.

Bonds lagged behind equities as investors engaged in selective buying after recent declines. The market movement came after concerns about technology firms at the center of the AI boom had driven stock prices lower in previous sessions, prompting renewed Middle East tensions to add to investor uncertainty.

cards.headline: Armed forces test humanoid robots for potential military use
cards.teaser: Military organizations are experimenting with humanoid robots, though deployment in combat remains years away.
cards.body:
Armed forces around the world are conducting experiments with humanoid robots as they explore potential military applications. The testing represents an early stage in evaluating whether such machines could eventually serve alongside human soldiers.

Battlefield deployment of humanoid robots remains distant, with significant technical and operational challenges still to overcome. The experiments focus on understanding the capabilities and limitations of humanoid form factors in military contexts, from logistics support to reconnaissance tasks.

hero.headline: Apple unveils AI-powered Siri upgrade at developer conference
hero.body:
Apple announced a major overhaul of its Siri digital assistant at its Worldwide Developers Conference on Monday, integrating the voice tool with the company's new artificial intelligence platform called Apple Intelligence. The upgraded Siri, set to launch in the fall, will function more like advanced AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini rather than a traditional search-based question-and-answer tool.

The announcement represents a significant shift in Apple's approach to artificial intelligence after years of delays and consumer frustration. The company has faced criticism for lagging behind competitors like Google in deploying AI features to its devices.

Mike Rockwell, Apple's vice-president of Siri engineering, explained that the company rebuilt Siri from the ground up with generative AI at its core. The redesigned assistant will have its own dedicated app and offer more conversational interactions. Powered by Google's Gemini AI model through a partnership between the two companies, the new Siri can access Apple's native app ecosystem on phones and computers to assist with planning, information retrieval and directions.

During a product demonstration, Rockwell showed how Siri identified a beach location from a photograph, then retrieved a friend's address and provided directions to the beach in Santa Cruz, California with a stop at the friend's house, all within the Siri interface. The tool will also handle proofreading, shopping, calendar management and camera functions like extracting nutrition information from food images. Initially, the service will only be available in English.

Alongside the Siri upgrade, Apple announced new child safety features designed to give parents greater control over their children's device use. The company acknowledged both the benefits of children having devices and the associated risks, particularly for children under 13. Parents will use an "easy-to-use setup assistant" to customize content their children can access and gradually expand permissions as they age.

New safeguards include requiring children to request permission before browsing unfamiliar websites in Safari and automatically blurring messages containing gore or violence. The screen time interface has been simplified to show parents which apps their children use and for how long. Parents can set daily time allowances either manually or following recommendations from the American Academy of Pediatrics, which Apple partnered with on these features.

The conference also featured updates to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, along with new Apple Intelligence features integrated into Safari, messaging and the Home app. Craig Federighi, Apple's senior vice-president of software engineering, addressed the company's previous lag in AI development, stating that some competitors appear to be "racing forward, seemingly pursuing AI for the sake of AI, without clear regard for the people that it's ultimately meant to serve."

The timing of these announcements comes after Apple agreed to settle a class-action lawsuit in May for $250 million, with some consumers receiving up to $95 in payouts over allegations that the company falsely advertised Siri's capabilities.

cards.headline: OpenAI files confidentially for public offering
cards.teaser: The AI company submitted a confidential filing to go public, intensifying its competition with rival Anthropic.
cards.body:
OpenAI has filed confidentially to go public on the US stock market, the company announced Monday. The artificial intelligence giant is expected to be valued at more than $850 billion, making it one of the most highly valued listings in market history. OpenAI acknowledged that the confidential filing would likely become public, so it chose to announce the move itself.

The company has not set a timeline for its public debut. OpenAI noted that there are advantages to remaining private for now, though going public could eventually become the best option depending on circumstances.

cards.teaser: The Federal Communications Commission lifted a deadline for Amazon's Leo satellite constellation project.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission granted Amazon a waiver that removes a deadline for deploying its Leo satellite broadband constellation. The FCC determined that the waiver serves the public interest by promoting the development of a second large satellite broadband network.

Amazon's Leo project aims to deliver internet access through a constellation of orbiting satellites. The waiver allows Amazon to proceed with its deployment plans without facing regulatory penalties for missing the original deadline.

cards.headline: Instagram adds feature to reorganize profile grids
cards.teaser: Meta rolled out a tool allowing Instagram users to rearrange posts on their profile pages.
cards.body:
Instagram has rolled out a widely available feature allowing users to rearrange posts on their profile grids. The capability became available on June 8th across both Android and iPhone mobile apps.

The tool gives users control over how their content appears to visitors, moving away from the previous reverse chronological display. The feature had been tested in limited groups before this wider release.

cards.headline: Sam Altman's identity verification company reduces staff
cards.teaser: Tools for Humanity, the eye-scanning identity verification firm, is conducting layoffs as it faces revenue challenges.
cards.body:
Tools for Humanity, Sam Altman's identity verification startup, is laying off staff as it struggles with revenue generation. The company uses iris-scanning technology to create unique digital identities for users.

The downsizing occurs as OpenAI, where Altman serves as CEO, moves forward with its initial public offering. Tools for Humanity has faced ongoing challenges in building a sustainable business model around its biometric verification platform.

cards.headline: Apple releases iOS 27 with new features and speed improvements
cards.teaser: The updated mobile operating system adds the ability to share phone numbers across devices and faster performance.
cards.body:
Apple announced iOS 27 at WWDC 2026, introducing practical features like the ability to share a single phone number across two iPhones and independent alarm volume controls. The update also delivers faster AirPlay connectivity and general performance improvements.

The new operating system maintains full support for existing iPhone models. Apple simultaneously released iPadOS 27, dropping support for only a small number of older iPad models. Both systems will roll out to users later this year following beta testing periods.

hero.headline: Spurs defeat Knicks 115-111 in Game 3 of NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the New York Knicks 115-111 in Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden on Monday night, snapping the Knicks' 13-game postseason winning streak and cutting the series deficit to 2-1.

Victor Wembanyama delivered his best performance of the Finals, finishing with 32 points, eight rebounds, six assists and three blocks. Stephon Castle added 23 points, including two crucial free throws with 6.8 seconds remaining in the contest. The Spurs' ability to execute in the closing moments proved decisive in what was described as a nail-biting finish.

The Knicks' Jalen Brunson led his team with 32 points while OG Anunoby contributed 28, but the rest of New York's roster struggled in the fourth quarter during a back-and-forth affair. The loss represented a significant setback for the home team, who had not lost since April 23.

The atmosphere at Madison Square Garden was extraordinary, with the spectacle surrounding the event nearly overshadowing the basketball itself. The game marked New York City's first home NBA Finals game since June 25, 1999. Tickets reportedly sold for as much as $10,000, and heightened security measures were implemented throughout the venue.

The event drew an array of notable attendees. Donald Trump, a longtime Knicks fan invited as a guest of team owner James Dolan, watched from a suite. When he appeared on the jumbotron during the national anthem, the crowd responded with loud boos and jeers. The president maintained a salute throughout the brief eight-second appearance. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani attended separately, having purchased a standing-room-only ticket for approximately $1,000.

Celebrity row featured an impressive lineup including Spike Lee, Timothée Chalamet, Ben Stiller, Tina Fey, Tracy Morgan and Larry David.

The Spurs' victory kept their championship hopes alive despite the historical odds against them. No NBA team has lost the first two games of the Finals on its home floor and successfully won the championship, but San Antonio demonstrated they can compete effectively in hostile territory.

The Knicks continue their pursuit of their first championship since 1973. Game 4 is scheduled for Wednesday in New York, where the series will continue with the Knicks holding a series advantage.

The win sparked celebrations in San Antonio, where heavy traffic was reported on highways following the Spurs' triumph. Both teams now prepare for the next contest, with momentum clearly shifting as the Finals continue.

cards.headline: Judge clears Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby to play despite NCAA gambling ban
cards.teaser: A court ruling allowed quarterback Brendan Sorsby to play for Texas Tech despite an NCAA ban for gambling violations, prompting criticism from rival coaches.
cards.body:
A judge has cleared Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby to play despite an NCAA ban imposed for gambling violations. The ruling has prompted strong reactions from coaches and athletic directors across college football, with TCU coach Sonny Dykes describing it as a bad day for the sport.

The decision has sparked significant backlash in college athletics. The Big Ten conference is reportedly discussing a potential league-wide ban on scheduling Texas Tech in all sports, while several schools are considering boycotting games against the team.

cards.headline: World Cup referee from Somalia denied entry to United States
cards.teaser: Omar Artan, who was set to become the first Somali referee at a World Cup finals, has been dropped from the officials list after being denied US entry.
cards.body:
Omar Artan, a prominent African referee from Somalia, has been barred from entering the United States and will not officiate at the 2026 World Cup. Artan was set to make history as the first Somali referee to work at a World Cup finals.

Following his denial of entry, Artan has been removed from FIFA's list of officials for the tournament, which will be co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The decision means the international referee roster for the competition has been adjusted accordingly.

cards.headline: Chiefs sign cornerback L'Jarius Sneed to one-year deal
cards.teaser: The Kansas City Chiefs signed veteran cornerback L'Jarius Sneed to a one-year contract worth up to $5 million, reuniting with the two-time Super Bowl winner.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

The Kansas City Chiefs signed cornerback L'Jarius Sneed to a one-year deal worth up to $5 million, according to his agents. Sneed previously won two Super Bowl championships with Kansas City before leaving the team.

The signing represents a reunion between Sneed and the Chiefs organization. The veteran cornerback returns to a familiar system as Kansas City looks to strengthen its defensive backfield. The deal brings an experienced player back to a team where he previously found success at the highest level of the sport.

cards.headline: Netherlands defender Jurrien Timber ruled out of World Cup with groin injury
cards.teaser: Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber has been ruled out of the Netherlands' World Cup campaign after sustaining a groin injury.
cards.body:
Jurrien Timber, Arsenal's defender, has been ruled out of the Netherlands' World Cup squad due to a groin injury. His absence is a significant blow to the Dutch team's defensive options as the tournament begins.

Meanwhile, Brazil's Neymar is making good progress in his recovery from injury, though his participation in the World Cup remains to be determined. Teams are navigating late injury setbacks as they finalize their squads for the competition.

cards.headline: England cricket captain Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson investigated over nightclub incident
cards.teaser: The England and Wales Cricket Board is investigating an incident at a nightclub involving captain Ben Stokes, bowler Gus Atkinson, and a Saracens academy player.
cards.body:
England cricket captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson are under investigation following a nightclub incident involving a Saracens academy player. The England and Wales Cricket Board is examining the matter alongside Premiership Rugby.

The investigation is ongoing and could affect the players' involvement in upcoming matches during the international season.

cards.headline: Scotland midfielder John McGinn in strong form ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Scotland midfielder John McGinn is performing at a high level as the national team prepares for the World Cup under manager Steve Clarke.
cards.body:
John McGinn is in exceptional form as Scotland prepares for the World Cup under manager Steve Clarke. The Aston Villa midfielder has impressed both on the pitch and in his media representations of the national team.

Scotland's World Cup preparations have been marked by controversy following the cancellation of a scheduled training match against Norway. The Scots postponed the friendly after Billy Gilmour suffered an injury during a recent friendly against Curaçao that ruled him out of the tournament. Norway criticized Scotland's decision, branding the move "unprofessional" and "weak," but McGinn defended the team's priorities, stating their job is to look after Scotland's interests.

hero.headline: Trump Booed at NBA Finals Game in New York
hero.body:
President Donald Trump received a loud, hostile reception at Madison Square Garden during Game 3 of the NBA Finals between the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks. When he appeared on the video screens during the National Anthem, thousands of basketball fans responded with sustained booing and jeering.

Trump was shown on the jumbotron for a little over eight seconds while the Star-Spangled Banner was being sung. He maintained a salute throughout his appearance and held a smile on his face as the crowd's disapproval echoed through the arena. The boos continued during the brief time he was displayed on screen. Once the video switched to show Knicks players lined up, the crowd's reaction shifted to cheers.

The president's appearance at the game made history. He became the first sitting U.S. president to attend the NBA Finals. The highly publicized visit to Madison Square Garden generated significant attention in advance of Game 3, with heightened security measures put in place for the event.

The arena took on an air of spectacle beyond the basketball itself. Trump watched from suites at the venue while various celebrities and dignitaries occupied other premium seating. The event had generated days of discussion about ticket prices, which reached $10,000, as well as security protocols and cancelled watch parties across the city.

This marked a rare public outing in New York City for Trump since taking office. His appearance at such a high-profile sporting event placed him directly in front of a national television audience, with his reception captured clearly on broadcast coverage.

The boos at Madison Square Garden add to a pattern of public appearances where Trump has encountered direct expressions of disapproval from live audiences. The NBA Finals represented one of the year's highest-profile sporting events, drawing millions of viewers and intense media coverage.

The crowd's vocal reaction was particularly striking given Trump's deep history with New York. He built a real estate and entertainment empire in the city before entering politics. Madison Square Garden has historically been a venue where political figures receive mixed reactions from diverse New York audiences.

Despite the likelihood of a negative reception, Trump chose to attend the Finals matchup in his hometown. The arena, known for hosting major sporting and entertainment events, became the scene of sustained public disapproval directed at the sitting president.

The incident occurred ahead of an exciting playoff series. The game itself ultimately saw the Spurs defeat the Knicks 115-111, with French center Victor Wembanyama delivering a dominant performance. The Knicks held a 2-1 series lead heading into Game 4.

cards.headline: Jon Stewart Criticizes Trump Over Meet the Press Interview Exit
cards.teaser: The Daily Show host addressed the president's decision to leave an interview after fact-checking by the host.
cards.body:
Jon Stewart used his platform on The Daily Show to criticize President Donald Trump for walking out of a recent Meet the Press interview. Stewart described Trump's exit as the reaction of someone unable to handle fact-checking from interviewer Kristen Welker.

The interview, which aired recently, ended when Trump left in response to persistent fact-checking by Welker during their conversation. Stewart's commentary aired during the episode that followed the interview, offering his assessment of the president's decision to end the session early rather than continue facing questions and corrections.

cards.headline: Cardi B Performs at NBA Finals Game 3 Halftime
cards.teaser: The rapper delivered a performance during the NBA Finals halftime show in New York.
cards.body:
Cardi B took the stage during halftime of Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden on Monday night. The rapper performed "Bodega Baddie" and "Bodak Yellow" for the crowd.

The game saw the San Antonio Spurs defeat the New York Knicks 115-111, with French star Victor Wembanyama leading the Spurs with 32 points. The Knicks maintain a 2-1 series lead.

cards.headline: Jason Momoa Exits Video Game Adaptation Helldivers
cards.teaser: The actor has left the PlayStation Productions project directed by Justin Lin.
cards.body:
Jason Momoa has left the Helldivers film project, a video game adaptation from PlayStation Productions and Sony Pictures directed by Justin Lin. The film is based on the franchise from Arrowhead Game Studios.

Sony Pictures is now searching for a replacement lead actor. The studio continues casting other roles as the project moves forward in development.

cards.headline: Documentary on Jean-Michel Basquiat Premieres at Tribeca Festival
cards.teaser: The film, acquired by Netflix, offers a comprehensive portrait of the artist's life.
cards.body:
A new documentary titled "Jean-Michel" premiered at the Tribeca Festival and was purchased by Netflix for distribution. Directed by Quinn Whitney Wilson and Viridiana Lieberman, the film presents a detailed examination of artist Jean-Michel Basquiat's life and work.

The documentary covers multiple aspects of Basquiat's life, from his upbringing in New York to his career as an artist. The film explores his development as a painter and his place in the downtown art scene, offering what reviewers describe as the first comprehensive documentary portrait of the artist.

cards.headline: Idris Elba Comments on Black Actor Playing James Bond
cards.teaser: The actor said audiences would not accept a Black actor in the role.
cards.body:
Idris Elba has dismissed speculation that he was seriously considered to play James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure. The 53-year-old actor told British GQ that the rumors linking him to the role were "never legit" while promoting his new film Masters of the Universe.

Elba stated that audiences would not accept a Black actor in the iconic spy role, suggesting it does not align with cultural expectations. He also expressed opposition to making the character "woke" in future casting decisions.

cards.headline: Farm Aid Announces Lineup for Virginia Beach Show
cards.teaser: Neil Young, Willie Nelson, and Dave Matthews will headline the benefit concert.
cards.body:
Farm Aid announced its 2026 Virginia Beach concert for September 26, featuring an eclectic mix of artists spanning generations. Neil Young and the Chrome Hearts will headline alongside Willie Nelson, Dave Matthews, and John Mellencamp.

The benefit concert supporting American farmers will also include performances by Margo Price and Jesse Welles, rounding out the multi-artist lineup for the annual charitable event.

hero.headline: Senate appropriations process stalls as parties fail to agree on spending totals
hero.body:
The Senate appropriations process has ground to a halt as Republicans and Democrats remain unable to reach agreement on overall spending levels. Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins stated that Democrats are not willing to work with Republicans on the issue.

The standoff threatens to delay the passage of annual funding bills that keep federal agencies and programs operating. Without agreement on top-line spending numbers, appropriations subcommittees cannot finalize individual spending measures for different government departments. The impasse reflects broader partisan divisions over federal spending priorities and budget levels.

The appropriations process typically begins after congressional leadership and the White House negotiate an overall budget framework that sets spending caps for discretionary programs. These negotiations establish the parameters within which appropriators can craft individual bills. The current deadlock suggests those preliminary negotiations have broken down or failed to produce a workable compromise.

Congress faces statutory deadlines for passing appropriations bills to avoid government shutdowns. When lawmakers cannot agree on full-year funding, they often resort to continuing resolutions that maintain spending at previous levels for limited periods. Such stopgap measures allow the government to keep operating but prevent agencies from starting new initiatives or adjusting to changed circumstances.

The Senate Appropriations Committee, one of the most powerful panels in Congress, oversees the drafting of twelve annual spending bills that together fund the entire discretionary federal budget. The committee's work requires bipartisan cooperation because appropriations bills need sixty votes to advance in the Senate. Collins, a Maine Republican, chairs the committee and has historically sought to build consensus across party lines on spending measures.

cards.headline: Republicans seek Trump retreat on intelligence nominee to preserve surveillance law
cards.teaser: Lawmakers hope the president will reconsider his intelligence director pick as they work to save expiring spy legislation.
cards.body:
President Trump has interviewed additional candidates for intelligence director as Republican lawmakers search for a way to preserve expiring surveillance authority. The interviews signal potential movement away from a previous nominee.

Lawmakers are seeking an alternative path forward that would allow crucial intelligence collection laws to continue. The surveillance authority in question provides legal framework for intelligence gathering activities.

cards.headline: House Republican targets end-of-month hearing for AI legislation
cards.teaser: Representative Jay Obernolte aims to advance his artificial intelligence proposal through committee before July.
cards.body:
Representative Jay Obernolte, who leads Republican efforts on artificial intelligence policy in the House, has set an ambitious timeline for advancing his legislative proposal. He expects a hearing on the bill could take place by the end of June.

Obernolte's legislation would establish federal policy governing artificial intelligence development and deployment. The California Republican has positioned himself as his party's lead voice on technology regulation in the lower chamber.

cards.headline: Democrats plan $30 million investment in state legislative races targeting House redistricting
cards.teaser: Super PAC Forward Majority will focus on two dozen statehouse contests that could influence congressional maps before 2028.
cards.body:
Democratic super PAC Forward Majority announced plans to spend $30 million on approximately two dozen state legislative races this election cycle. The group believes as few as eight statehouse contests could determine control of redistricting processes affecting six U.S. House seats ahead of 2028.

Leslie Martes, Forward Majority's chief executive officer, described the current redistricting environment as the Wild West. The investment reflects Democratic strategy to influence congressional maps at the state level, where district boundaries are drawn. The United States has 7,000 state legislative districts, though not all face elections this year.

cards.headline: Becerra and Hilton advance to California governor general election
cards.teaser: Former state attorney general Xavier Becerra will face Trump-endorsed Steve Hilton in November race to succeed Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Former California Attorney General Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, a former Fox News host, will compete in the November general election for governor. Decision Desk HQ projected both candidates advanced from the primary.

Hilton secured Republican support with an endorsement from President Trump, while the Democratic field remained divided among multiple candidates. Becerra previously served as California's top law enforcement official before the governor's race.

cards.headline: Vice President Vance questions Los Angeles mayoral primary outcome
cards.teaser: Vance called the result of the LA mayor's race, which will feature two Democrats in November, pretty shady.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance said Monday that the Los Angeles mayoral primary result appeared "pretty shady" to him. The race will proceed to November's general election with two Democratic candidates: Mayor Karen Bass and Los Angeles Councilmember Nithya Raman, who defeated other candidates in the primary.

Vance's comments bring federal political scrutiny to a municipal election. The race is expected to feature tensions within the Democratic party as the two Democrats compete against each other in the general election.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. She previously served in the Biden administration before launching her gubernatorial campaign.

If Haaland wins the general election, she would make history as the first female Native American to serve as a state governor. The general election will take place in November.
